c.tagline: Canals, palazzos, and light on the water

emergency.note: 112 is the universal EU number; 113 police and 118 ambulance also work, and English is often available.

hood_landmark.San Marco: St Mark's Basilica on Piazza San Marco
hood_landmark.Cannaregio: the historic Jewish Ghetto and its synagogues
hood_landmark.Dorsoduro: Basilica di Santa Maria della Salute at the Grand Canal's mouth
hood_landmark.Castello: the Arsenale shipyards and Biennale gardens
hood_landmark.San Polo: the Rialto Bridge and its centuries-old market

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around San Marco/Rialto and on vaporetti; overpriced-restaurant scams

hood_desc: San Marco is the glamorous heart of Venice around St. Mark's Square and Basilica, home to luxury hotels, designer shops and top sights, ideal for first-timers and upscale stays despite the crowds.
Cannaregio is a lively, more residential sestiere with the historic Jewish Ghetto, canal-side bars and local trattorias, great for authentic atmosphere and better value.
Dorsoduro is the artsy, student district of the Accademia and Guggenheim museums, buzzing Campo Santa Margherita nightlife and calmer canals, suited to culture lovers and younger travelers.
Castello is the largest, most local sestiere east of San Marco, quieter and residential with the Arsenale and Biennale gardens, appealing to travelers seeking everyday Venetian life.
San Polo is the bustling market district around the Rialto Bridge and Rialto Market, full of bacari wine bars and shops, perfect for foodies and central sightseeing.
lodging: Danieli, Venezia, A Four Seasons Hotel

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink; public fountains (acqua alta) also run drinkable water.

transit.pay: A single vaporetto ride costs 9.50 EUR (~US$11), so most visitors buy 1/2/3/7-day passes (25/35/45/65 EUR) from ACTV-Venezia Unica machines and booths at Piazzale Roma, the station and main stops. You can also just tap a contactless bank card at the 'Tappy' validators each time you board — the system charges the best fare with a daily cap. Always validate or tap before boarding.
transit.hours: Main lines (1, 2, and the Murano/Burano routes) run about 5am-midnight; night line N covers the Grand Canal and Lido overnight.
transit.note: The vaporetto IS the transit — Venice has no cars or bikes, so it's boats or your own two feet. Buses and trams only serve Mestre and the Lido.

transit.m: ATVO airport bus to Piazzale Roma (25 min)
Alilaguna water bus to St. Mark's and Grand Canal stops (75 min)

food.name: Cicchetti
food.desc: Small bar snacks eaten standing with a glass of wine: crostini, fried morsels, marinated seafood. The heart of Venetian bacaro culture.

places.name: Cantina Do Mori
places.note: One of the oldest bacari in Venice, hung with copper pots; cash-friendly and tiny.

places.name: Bar All'Arco
places.note: Father-and-son counter near Rialto market, a genuine locals' stop.

places.name: Cantine del Vino gia Schiavi
places.note: Institution by the gondola yard with dozens of inventive crostini.

food.name: Sarde in saor
food.desc: Fried sardines marinated in vinegar with sweet onions, raisins and pine nuts. A sailors' preserve, best after a day or two of resting.

places.name: Bar All'Arco
places.note: Among the most ordered cicchetti here; made fresh from the market next door.

places.name: Osteria Bancogiro
places.note: Canal-side former bank building with all-day service and Grand Canal tables.

places.name: Cantina Do Mori
places.note: Traditional version at the counter, paired with an ombra of local white.

food.name: Baccala mantecato
food.desc: Stockfish whipped with olive oil into a pale, airy cream, spread on grilled white polenta. Venice's most beloved cicchetto.

places.name: Cantine del Vino gia Schiavi
places.note: Silky version on crostini, eaten standing outside by the canal.

places.name: Antiche Carampane
places.note: Hidden fish restaurant with no-tourist-menu attitude; reserve ahead.

places.name: Bar All'Arco
places.note: Small counter with a strong local wine list to match the baccala.

food.name: Risotto al nero di seppia
food.desc: Inky black risotto cooked with cuttlefish and its own ink, deeply savoury and unmistakably lagoon food.

places.name: Osteria Boccadoro
places.note: Quiet campo setting; the squid-ink risotto is its best-known plate.

places.name: Osteria alle Testiere
places.note: Nine tables, market-driven seafood menu, two sittings a night by reservation.

places.name: Antiche Carampane
places.note: Long-standing family kitchen doing classic lagoon dishes properly.

food.name: Fritto misto and moeche
food.desc: Lagoon seafood fried light: calamari, prawns and small fish, plus soft-shell crabs in the short spring and autumn moeche seasons.

places.name: Trattoria alla Madonna
places.note: Bustling 1954 fish house near the bridge, big rooms and quick service.

places.name: Osteria Bancogiro
places.note: Fried lagoon fish steps from the market where the catch is bought.

places.name: Antiche Carampane
places.note: Seasonal moeche when they run; ask what came in that morning.

food.name: Fegato alla veneziana
food.desc: Calf's liver cooked slowly with sweet onions and a splash of vinegar, served with soft or grilled polenta. A Venetian classic since the 1500s.

places.name: Vini da Gigio
places.note: Canal-side family restaurant with an outstanding wine cellar; book ahead.

places.name: Trattoria alla Madonna
places.note: Old-school kitchen that has kept the traditional recipe unchanged.

places.name: Osteria Boccadoro
places.note: Neighbourhood address away from the crowds, strong on Venetian standards.

food.name: Spritz
food.desc: Prosecco, soda and a bitter, over ice with an olive. Venetians favour the local Select bitter over Aperol; Campari makes it drier.

places.name: Osteria al Squero
places.note: Drink on the canal wall opposite the historic gondola boatyard.

places.name: Al Timon
places.note: Fondamenta della Misericordia favourite; sit on the moored boat outside.

places.name: Cantine del Vino gia Schiavi
places.note: Spritz and ombre poured all day to a mixed local and student crowd.

food.name: Bellini
food.desc: White peach puree topped with prosecco, invented in Venice in the 1940s and named after the painter's rosy skies.

places.name: Harry's Bar
places.note: Where the Bellini was created; expensive, but the original recipe.

places.name: Bar Longhi
places.note: Gritti Palace bar with Grand Canal terrace and immaculate service.

landmarks: St. Mark's Basilica
A dazzling Byzantine-style cathedral covered in gold mosaics that anchors the grandeur of St. Mark's Square.
St. Mark's Square (Piazza San Marco)
Venice's grand civic heart, ringed by arcades and cafes and famously prone to atmospheric flooding reflections.
Doge's Palace
The ornate Gothic palace that once housed Venice's rulers, its pink-and-white facade iconic along the lagoon.
Rialto Bridge
The oldest and most famous bridge spanning the Grand Canal, lined with shops and bustling with gondolas below.
Grand Canal
Venice's main waterway, flanked by centuries-old palazzi and best experienced by gondola or vaporetto at sunset.
Bridge of Sighs
A romantic enclosed limestone bridge said to be the last sight prisoners had of Venice before imprisonment.
Burano Island
A short boat ride from Venice, famous for its vividly painted fishermen's houses lining tiny canals.
Murano Island
The historic center of Venetian glassmaking, with colorful canals and glowing glass-blowing furnaces.
Santa Maria della Salute
A monumental Baroque church with a striking white domed silhouette marking the entrance to the Grand Canal.
Ca' d'Oro
A jewel-like Gothic palace on the Grand Canal renowned for its intricate lace-like marble facade.

train.note: International trains use Venezia Santa Lucia (on the island) and also call at Venezia Mestre. From December 2025 the daytime Vienna Railjets run a faster route via Graz. Domestic high-speed is Trenitalia or Italo (italotreno.com).

bus.note: Coaches leave from Tronchetto or Venezia Mestre, not the historic centre - check your ticket.

ferry.note: Fast catamarans to Istria run roughly April-October from the San Basilio/Venice ferry terminals. The old long-haul ferries to Greece no longer sail from Venice - the nearest Greece crossings leave from Ancona.

half.name: Murano & Burano
half.blurb: Lagoon islands famed for glassblowing artistry and rainbow-painted fishermen's houses along quiet canals.

half.name: Verona
half.blurb: Romeo and Juliet's romantic city, home to a magnificent Roman amphitheater and elegant piazzas.

half.name: Padua
half.blurb: A lively university city with Giotto's frescoes, ancient markets, and grand arcaded streets.

half.name: Vicenza
half.blurb: An elegant Renaissance city showcasing Palladio's celebrated villas and graceful classical architecture.

half.name: Treviso
half.blurb: A pretty canal-laced town with frescoed houses, arcades, and the birthplace of tiramisu.

half.name: Prosecco Hills
half.blurb: Rolling UNESCO vineyards producing Italy's beloved sparkling wine amid postcard rural scenery.
